cases.article_title: Banner protest over 18-month wait for disabled bay
cases.disability_connection: A disabled parking space and wheelchair access for a woman whose mobility is declining while she is terminally ill with a brain tumour.

source_access.method: Direct HTTPS retrieval from the canonical BBC URL returned HTTP 200 and the publisher article body on 2026-11-01.

evidence.text: Paul Rapetti installed a 16ft banner outside his Lincoln home in frustration over an 18-month wait for a decision on a disabled parking space for his wife Berta, who is terminally ill with a brain tumour.
He applied in March 2025 and, despite being told a decision would take weeks, nothing had been decided when the article was published.
The banner said a disabled person lived there and asked motorists to leave a space; he also asked neighbours to leave room for their car and wheelchair access.
Lincolnshire County Council's highways executive member said officers would review the situation and provide a recommendation so a decision could be made; this was not an approval or rejection.
Berta's mobility was declining and she wanted the matter resolved.

cases.article_title: Paid Commission for DPOs | Contribute to sector-changing research on DPO Funding
cases.disability_connection: Research into funding for Disabled People's Organisations and participation by DPOs.

source_access.method: Direct retrieval from the canonical Disability Rights UK URL returned the publisher page and article body on 2026-11-01.

evidence.text: Trust for London, Disability Rights UK and Braw Data are collaborating on a UK-wide research project mapping funding to the disability sector.

The partners state that the project is intended to support campaigners promoting funding justice for Disabled People's Organisations and led-by-and-for organisations; the source does not establish that funding justice has already improved.
Disabled People's Organisations are invited to complete a 30-minute online form confirming their classification and funding sources and are offered £50 for 30 minutes.
The article describes the project as sector-changing and presents a funding tool and DPO map as future outputs; these are promotional or intended claims, not independently achieved outcomes.
evidence.source_location: DRUK promotional description and future-output wording
